items.name: Recovery test — Arpio snapshot recovery (dev)
preconditions: Phase 0 checklist green and signed off
Recovery scope re-selected and saved in Arpio within the last week
Operator and approver both on the calendar for the full window
T0 definition agreed: T0 = recovery launch initiated in Arpio

steps.title: Pre-flight: record T0 and recovery-point alignment
steps.detail: Open the test record and write wall-clock T0 the moment recovery is initiated. Confirm recovery points for all protected resources (Aurora ×3, S3, SQS, ECR, secrets) come from the same aligned sync set. Screenshot the list — this is the RPA evidence.
steps.verify: Every in-scope resource shows a recovery point from the same sync, none older than 30 min
steps.pass: Aligned points within RPO; screenshot in the record

steps.title: Pre-flight: confirm sandbox/network flags
steps.detail: Per the standing decision, sandbox/isolated networking is OFF so image pulls and secrets-init have real egress. Confirm the launch settings before starting — the July dry run lost 90 minutes to this.
steps.verify: Flags match the test plan (sandbox OFF, production guards ON)
steps.pass: Flags confirmed by approver on the bridge

steps.title: Launch ops account first (ECR before apps)
steps.detail: Start recovery of the ops account so the 17 ECR repositories exist in us-east-2 before any app pod tries to pull. Ops app before Dev app — ordering is mandatory.
steps.verify: ECR repositories appearing in us-east-2 with expected tags

steps.title: Launch application account
steps.detail: Start recovery of the app environment (VPC, EKS, Aurora ×3, Redis, SQS, S3, secrets) from the aligned recovery points. Cold-start duration from here is the number leadership asks about — last measured ~40 min.
steps.verify: Recovery job progressing; resources appearing in dependency order

steps.title: Verify platform: nodes, mesh, DNS, controllers
steps.detail: Nodes Ready, CoreDNS resolving, istiod up, ALB controller and Karpenter running. Do not look at app pods yet — a broken platform makes every app failure a red herring.
steps.command: kubectl get nodes && kubectl get pods -n kube-system && kubectl get pods -n istio-system
steps.verify: All nodes Ready; CoreDNS/istiod/ALB controller/Karpenter Running

steps.title: Verify data layer: Aurora + queues restored and fresh
steps.detail: From a pod in the recovery VPC, connect to each Aurora cluster and run the freshness query. Age at T0 = measured RPA (last test: 118 min against a 30 min config). Confirm SQS queues exist; in-flight loss is accepted and documented.
steps.verify: All three Aurora clusters answer; freshness recorded per DB
steps.pass: Data reachable; RPA numbers in the record

steps.title: Verify secrets: every logical name resolves (tests die HERE)
steps.detail: Before any app starts, walk the signed-off secret list against us-east-2 Secrets Manager. This is where the August test failed: two adjudication secrets missing → secrets-init crash loops an hour later. Check the list, not your memory.
steps.command: for s in $(cat signed-off-secrets.txt); do aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id "$s" --region us-east-2 >/dev/null || echo "MISSING: $s"; done
steps.pass: Every logical name resolves; no ResourceNotFoundException

steps.title: Verify applications: pods up, images from us-east-2 registry
steps.detail: Confirm adjudication, remittance, pharmacy, pricing all Ready — and that every image reference points at the us-east-2 registry. A pod pulling cross-region from us-east-1 passes the test and fails the disaster.
steps.command: kubectl get deploy -A && kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}' | sort -u
steps.verify: Tier-0/1 deployments Ready; zero images referencing us-east-1

steps.title: Verify edge WITHOUT touching DNS
steps.detail: Hit the recovered API Gateway execute-api endpoint directly with a Host header for the real domain. Public DNS is never changed in Phase 1.
steps.verify: HTTP 200 through API GW → VPC Link → NLB → recovered pods

steps.title: Success bar 1: test claim answered end-to-end
steps.detail: Submit the partner-shaped test claim against the direct endpoint. A real adjudication response with a claim_id — not a 500 — is what 'recovered' means. First success = T1.
steps.pass: Claim adjudicated end-to-end; T1 recorded; RTA = T1 − T0

steps.title: Success bar 2: settlement path runs
steps.detail: Kick the remittance import against the recovered bucket/queue and confirm rows land in the recovered remittance Aurora. Front-door success with a dead settlement path is still an outage for finance.
steps.command: kubectl -n remittance create job --from=cronjob/era-import dr-test-import && kubectl logs -f job/dr-test-import
steps.verify: Import completes; rows in recovered remittance DB

steps.title: Conclude: no failback without explicit approval
steps.detail: Teardown/conclude only on the approver's written go — failback semantics can have production side effects and the standing decision forbids reflexive failback during tests.
steps.verify: Written approval from the named approver in the channel

steps.title: Triage findings same-day: gaps, tickets, runbook edits
steps.detail: Write the record while it hurts. Every surprise becomes a gap with severity, a ticket, or an edit to this runbook — usually all three.
steps.verify: Every finding has a gap id or ticket next to it
steps.pass: Record written same day; findings filed

rollback.title: Tear down the recovered test environment
rollback.detail: After approval, conclude the recovery in Arpio so us-east-2 test resources are destroyed and replication resumes. Verify replication returns to green — a test that leaves replication broken has negative value.
rollback.verify: Recovery-region test resources gone; replication green
rollback.pass: Protected + replicating; no orphaned us-east-2 resources billing

items.notes: Instantiated from the arpio-recovery-test template. Phase 1 only — DNS and live traffic untouched. The August run died at step 7 (secrets); the signed-off list now exists and must be re-verified before the September run.
